text: Continuous integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. The main idea is that developers regularly add their code changes to a shared repository. Each time this happens, automated builds start automatically, which means the software is compiled without anyone doing it by hand. The system also runs tests to check that the new code works correctly and does not break anything. This helps teams catch issues early, when they are still easy and cheap to fix. Many companies use CI pipelines, which are a series of steps that build, test, and sometimes deploy the code. As a result, software quality improves and releases become faster and safer.
